headline: Pilbara Minerals surges 7.9% on a blockbuster FY26 result as gold hits record highs and global markets hold steady.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS rocketed 7.9% today after releasing its FY26 full-year results — revenue surged 152% as the lithium market recovers from its brutal lows. The company returned to profit and flagged a bullish outlook on lithium prices, with expansion plans on the table. The market loved it.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG edged up 1.05% in last night's session, supported by strong Q2 2026 earnings and continued momentum in AI products. The market is rewarding Alphabet for holding its ground in the AI race alongside Microsoft.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT gained 0.43% last night as the stock consolidates after a big AI-driven earnings surge earlier in the year. No major news — just steady confidence in its AI cloud business (Azure and Copilot).

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped 1.35% today, which is the biggest drag in the portfolio this session. Emerging markets are sensitive to global risk appetite and a stronger Aussie dollar (which hurts foreign asset values when converted back). No specific single-country crisis — just general caution.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI dipped a modest 0.43% today. The AI ETF is still sitting 14.6% below your cost basis — a reminder that concentrated tech/AI themes can be volatile. No specific news today driving the move; broader market softness in the AI sector.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS edged down 0.23% today. This ASX-listed ETF mirrors the entire US share market, and the small dip reflects the slight lag from last night's flat-ish US session. A very minor move — nothing to read into.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO slipped 0.22% last night — barely a move. There's noise around a GTA 6 gameplay video leak, with Take-Two taking legal action to identify the leaker and seek account records through the courts. A former Rockstar director has called the leaks a 'nothing burger'. The GTA 6 hype cycle is very much intact.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG crept up 0.14% today — steady as she goes. This diversified fund tracks global and Australian shares, so it moves with the broad market. A quiet, positive session with no specific catalyst.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Blockbuster FY26 result, up 7.9% today
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals delivered a stunning FY26 result — revenue up 152%, back in profit, and management is bullish on the lithium price outlook with expansion plans flagged. The stock is still 18.8% below your cost basis overall, but this is exactly the recovery you've been waiting for. Long-term thesis intact and strengthening — sit tight or consider topping up.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — Still underwater, but AI sector holding
watch_today.detail: GXAI is your biggest loss position at -14.6% overall and dipped another 0.43% today. That said, the global AI sector remains a major structural growth theme — Alphabet and Microsoft (both in your portfolio) are performing well, and global AI regulation discussions are intensifying which could eventually shape the playing field. For a long-term holder, the case for AI exposure hasn't changed. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: Gold hits ~$4,695 USD/oz — a new record high
watch_today.detail: Gold surged 1.53% last night to nearly $4,695 an ounce. It's being driven by geopolitical tension (US-Iran sanctions standoff, Middle East uncertainty) and a general flight to safe assets. You don't hold gold directly, but rising gold prices often signal broader risk-off sentiment — worth watching to see if it spills into equities.

watch_today.title: GOOG — Earnings momentum carrying the stock higher
watch_today.detail: GOOG is up 1.05% last night and sitting 11.2% above your cost basis. Strong Q2 2026 earnings and AI momentum are driving the valuation. Nothing to do here — this is working as a long-term hold.

watch_today.title: RBA rate cut signals building — watch for AUD moves
watch_today.detail: HSBC is calling the end of the RBA's hiking cycle based on the latest jobs data, and the AUD has already ticked up 0.63% to $0.7164 USD. A stronger Aussie dollar slightly reduces the AUD value of your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) when converted back. Nothing dramatic — just keep an eye on this as the RBA story develops.

watch_today.title: MSFT — Consolidating after big AI surge
watch_today.detail: Microsoft is up 0.43% last night and 9.1% above your cost basis. Stock is in consolidation mode after a strong earnings run — that's healthy. No reason to touch it.

world.summary: The US midterm election cycle is heating up with Trump raising doubts about election integrity, Iran is pushing back hard on new US sanctions while its president signals openness to a peace path, and Iran has also announced a major new gas discovery. A tense and complex week on the world stage.

stories.title: Trump casts doubt on US election integrity ahead of midterms
stories.why_it_matters: With US midterm elections approaching, Donald Trump has continued to publicly question the integrity of the electoral process, according to The Guardian. Experts are watching closely and warning that such rhetoric — if it leads to attempts to interfere with or contest results — could trigger serious constitutional and democratic instability in the world's largest economy. Democrats and their allies are reportedly preparing contingency plans. US political uncertainty tends to spook financial markets globally, including the ASX.

stories.title: Democrats prepare for possible Trump interference in midterm elections
stories.why_it_matters: The Los Angeles Times reports that Democratic party officials and allied organisations are actively building legal and organisational defences against potential interference in the upcoming midterm elections. The concern is that Trump could attempt to pressure state officials or contest results in close races. For global markets, a contested US election outcome would be a significant source of volatility — think late 2020, but potentially more disruptive.

stories.title: Iran calls US sanction threats 'desperate' — but president hints at deal
stories.why_it_matters: Iran's foreign minister dismissed new threatened US economic sanctions as 'desperate', while simultaneously Iran's president said a US memorandum could be the best path out of the stalled war — sending mixed signals. The tension matters because Iran sits on massive oil and gas reserves; any escalation can push global oil prices higher. Oil actually fell 1.67% last night to $85.61/barrel, suggesting markets aren't pricing in imminent escalation — but watch this space.

stories.title: Iran announces major new gas reserves discovery
stories.why_it_matters: Iran has disclosed a significant new natural gas discovery, which could further complicate global energy markets if and when sanctions are eventually lifted and Iran can ramp up exports. For now, with sanctions in place, the gas stays in the ground — but it signals Iran's long-term energy leverage in any future negotiation. Long term, more global gas supply is deflationary for energy prices.

markets.summary: A broadly positive session last night in the US, with both the S&P 500 and NASDAQ up around 0.43%. The ASX 200 followed suit today, closing up 0.49% at 9,103. Gold surged to nearly $4,695/oz — a fresh record — on geopolitical uncertainty. Oil fell 1.67% to $85.61/barrel. The Aussie dollar strengthened, climbing to US$0.7164.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Solid session today — up 44 points, lifted by resources and broad optimism.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Steady gains last night in the US — markets holding near record highs.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech stocks held firm last night, supported by AI optimism and solid earnings from big tech.

indicators.name: Gold (WTI)
indicators.note: Gold hit a fresh record high last night — geopolitical tension and safe-haven demand driving the run.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil dropped last night — markets not pricing in major Middle East escalation despite Iran-US tensions.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar strengthened — traders betting the RBA is close to done with rate rises.

politics.summary: The Albanese government is moving to take control of AI data centre energy rules away from the states, the ACTU is clashing with the Reserve Bank over wages and inflation, and Australia's big banks are hiking fees ahead of a looming card surcharge ban.

stories.title: Albanese to override Queensland on AI data centre energy rules
stories.why_it_matters: The federal government is planning to set national energy rules for AI data centres, overriding a defiant Queensland government that wanted to set its own standards. Data centres are power-hungry facilities that could strain the electricity grid — getting the energy rules right matters for the cost and reliability of power for everyday Aussies. It also signals Canberra is getting serious about the AI infrastructure buildout, which has major implications for energy investment.

stories.title: HSBC calls the end of the RBA rate hiking cycle after latest jobs data
stories.why_it_matters: HSBC's economists say the latest Australian jobs figures suggest the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA — the body that sets official interest rates) is likely done raising rates. If true, this is good news for mortgage holders and borrowers who've been squeezed by rising repayments since 2022. It's also one reason the Aussie dollar ticked higher today — markets are adjusting their expectations for future rate moves.

stories.title: ACTU wages push puts it on collision course with the RBA
stories.why_it_matters: The ACTU (Australia's peak union body) is pushing hard for higher wages, putting it in direct conflict with the RBA, which worries that big wage rises could reignite inflation. The AFR reports the ACTU has also cut the RBA's access to certain economic data as part of the dispute. Higher wages are good for workers but could delay any interest rate cuts if the RBA fears a wage-price spiral — worth watching.

stories.title: Big banks hiking fees and slashing rewards ahead of card surcharge ban
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's major banks are raising fees and cutting credit card rewards programs ahead of a government ban on card surcharges. The ban is meant to stop merchants from slugging customers with extra fees for paying by card — but the banks are effectively recouping lost revenue through the back door by hiking annual fees and reducing rewards. If you hold a rewards credit card, it's worth checking if your benefits have been trimmed.

ai.summary: AI regulation is the dominant theme in global tech policy right now — from Canberra's data centre energy rules to the EU's approach, a US congressional discussion on containment failures, and a new healthcare AI sandbox being tested. Meanwhile, a new coding AI model called Ox Alpha has emerged.

stories.title: Critics say Albanese isn't up to Australia's AI challenge
stories.why_it_matters: The Nightly is running commentary arguing that Prime Minister Albanese lacks a coherent, bold national strategy to manage the AI boom — at a time when Australia needs to make big decisions about data infrastructure, energy, jobs and regulation. The federal government's move to override Queensland on data centre energy rules today suggests some action is happening, but critics say it's reactive rather than visionary. For investors, Australia's AI policy settings matter for how quickly local AI-linked companies and ETFs (like your GXAI) can benefit from the global boom.

stories.title: US Congress holds hearing on AI regulation and containment failures
stories.why_it_matters: US lawmakers held a formal discussion on AI regulation and what happens when AI 'containment' measures fail — meaning when AI systems behave in unintended or dangerous ways. The fact that Congress is holding these hearings signals that formal US AI regulation (currently very light-touch) may be coming. Tighter rules in the US could reshape the business models of major AI companies like Alphabet and Microsoft.

stories.title: Healthcare AI sandbox — the next regulatory test is autonomous medicine
stories.why_it_matters: Regulators are trialling an AI 'sandbox' in healthcare — a controlled environment where AI tools can be tested for diagnosing and treating patients before being let loose on the general public. The next big question is whether to allow fully autonomous AI medical decisions (without a human doctor sign-off). This matters because healthcare AI is one of the biggest potential growth areas for companies like Alphabet (which has significant healthcare AI projects through DeepMind).

stories.title: Ox Alpha emerges as a powerful new AI coding model
stories.why_it_matters: A new AI model called Ox Alpha has emerged as a strong performer specifically for writing and understanding code. The AI coding space is getting very crowded — with GitHub Copilot (Microsoft), Gemini Code (Google), and now new challengers like Ox Alpha. Competition here is fierce, which is both a risk (pricing pressure) and a signal of how much value the market sees in AI-assisted software development. Relevant to both your MSFT and GOOG holdings.

sport.summary: Wests Tigers pulled off the upset of the NRL season on the weekend, and the AFL's wildcard finals schedule has been locked in. Joey Manu's long-anticipated NRL return has been confirmed with the new PNG Chiefs team. Round 26 NRL kicks off Thursday with Broncos vs Storm at Suncorp.

stories.title: Tigers stun first-place Roosters in 79th-minute upset of the year
stories.why_it_matters: Wests Tigers produced arguably the upset of the 2026 NRL season, defeating first-placed Sydney Roosters with a 79th-minute winner. Fox Sports is reporting on the verdict on a Roosters star following the loss. The Roosters will now face the Dolphins at Allianz Stadium in Round 26 Saturday — a must-watch game to see if they bounce back. The Tigers face the Cowboys up in Townsville on Saturday night.

stories.title: Joey Manu confirmed to return to NRL with new PNG Chiefs franchise
stories.why_it_matters: Joey Manu's NRL return has been locked in — he'll sign with the new PNG Chiefs franchise as their marquee '007' signing. Manu, a star centre/fullback who left the Roosters, is a major coup for the expansion team. Reports suggest rival clubs could get him even earlier if a deal is brought forward. The PNG Chiefs are set to join the NRL competition and Manu's signing puts them on the map immediately.

stories.title: AFL Wildcard Round schedule confirmed — finals fixture revealed
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL has confirmed its Wildcard Round fixtures, giving fans the full week two finals schedule. Fremantle is reportedly not feared by the Hawks heading in, while Melbourne (Dees) is being labelled the biggest loser of Round 24. The Wildcard Round adds an extra layer of excitement to the finals series — more teams get a second chance, meaning the premiership race is very much alive for multiple clubs.

stories.title: Sydney Swans crisis deepens over fresh allegation
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Swans are facing a deepening off-field crisis, with a fresh allegation reported by News.com.au today. With the AFL finals approaching, any significant off-field drama at a finals-bound club can affect team cohesion, selections, and public support. Details of the specific allegation aren't yet fully detailed in available reporting, but the story is developing quickly.
